epic.summary: makato suite harness independence — makato-oss fork on the oh-my-pi runtime
epic.objective: Make the makato suite harness- and vendor-independent by forking it onto the open-source oh-my-pi runtime (makato-oss), running primarily open models cross-platform on Linux/Vast.ai, while the production Claude Code makato stays untouched as version fallback.
epic.testTopology: Claude Code on the Mac is only the EDITOR used to author/commit makato-oss — it is NOT the test target. makato-oss is exercised by running the oh-my-pi (omp) runtime, which is cross-platform (D6). Three test targets: (T1) Mac local — omp on macOS against a cloud open-model API, fast dev loop, no GPU; (T2) no-GPU Linux VM — Lima/UTM on the Mac or a cheap Vast.ai CPU instance, for OS-portability + persistent-volume + systemd + network-partition work; (T3) Vast.ai A6000 GPU instance — the ONLY GPU-required target, for the on-instance vLLM + co-located sagibeast + Langfuse stack. Each story carries a description.testTarget naming which of T1/T2/T3 applies.

stories.summary: Fork bootstrap + Phase-0 spike: headless omp dispatch on an open model

description.background: makato-oss is a point-in-time fork of makato into a new repo + GitHub project (D3, big-bang on copy). The walking skeleton proves the oh-my-pi harness can drive makato skills headlessly on an open model before any dispatch rewrite commits. It also resolves the three open questions the whole dispatch design hangs on: the phase-detection contract (D16/Q-spike), the empirical skill-migration scope (Q5), and the filterBrowser MCP caveat (Q8).
description.scope: Create the makato-oss fork (repo + GitHub project) as the entry-point enabler. Stand up a minimal single-open-endpoint models.yml. Run omp --yolo -p headless against 3 representative skills (prompt-only / MCP-calling / sub-agent-dispatch). Capture the omp --mode rpc terminal-event shape AND the resume-handle equivalent, then commit a decision doc that flips Decision 3 (D16) from PENDING to a fixed contract (Option A RPC-adapter vs Option B state-file-only). Measure how many of the ~25 agent files need harness-specific change beyond a modelRole substitution. Explicitly verify Playwright MCP resolves from a sub-agent (filterBrowser gate, Q8). State an explicit pass/fail gate: if oh-my-pi fails the headless/sub-agent/MCP contract, the Hermes fallback (D2) is triggered before S2–S4 commit.
description.testTarget: T1 Mac (omp local, cloud open-model API) for the 3-skill smoke + RPC-shape capture, then a confirming headless run on a T2 no-GPU Linux VM. No GPU and no Vast.ai instance needed — the spike is about the harness contract, not the model host.

stories.summary: loop.sh dispatches the po-agent via oh-my-pi instead of claude -p

description.background: The deepest Claude Code coupling is the dispatch invocation. loop.sh must launch the po-agent through the oh-my-pi headless contract instead of claude -p, using the phase-detection contract fixed in sequence 1.
description.scope: Rename MAKATO_CLAUDE_BIN -> MAKATO_HARNESS_BIN (loop.sh:264) and re-point it to omp. Replace the claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions --output-format stream-json invocation (loop.sh:5208) with omp --yolo -p. Re-express _parse_dispatch_result (loop.sh:2450) and _extract_session_id per the D16 contract from sequence 1. Preserve the watchdog liveness check and the MAKATO_HEADLESS=1 guard. Resume-handle contingency: if sequence 1 shows omp has no session-resume analogue, stall-recovery is replaced by watchdog-timeout + reconcile with no resume (state-file path only) and this story is re-scoped and re-estimated accordingly.
description.testTarget: T1 Mac (omp local, cloud open endpoint) — a bash-level dispatch change; grep audit + one live dispatch is OS-independent, no GPU.

This story blocks the MVP proof (sequence 5) whose acceptance requires every step on an open endpoint — so it is foundation-tier despite being config work.

Verify the harness routes each role to the open endpoint (subset live-dispatch smoke per role type). Confirm the per-step modelRole->endpoint tag is emittable (integration point needed by sequence 10).

stories.summary: Cross-platform portability remediation + state/transcript path re-homing

description.background: makato-oss is cross-platform (macOS + Linux), not a macOS->Linux port (D6). The runtime path must carry zero unguarded darwin-isms — detect-and-branch, not swap — and re-home the hardcoded session-transcript path the Langfuse hook reads.
description.scope: Detect-and-branch the osascript HALT notifier (loop-halt-watch.sh:43); keep the portable flock/mutex, readlink -f python fallback, stat -c/-f branch, _guarded_sleep, and BSD-safe sed (already cross-platform). Add a new MAKATO_TRANSCRIPT_PATH env override + an oh-my-pi transcript-path adapter for the one hardcoded path (loop.sh:4711) so the Langfuse hook can consume it. Re-home HALT/state/specs/config via the existing env overrides; interim default is a local state dir (the persistent-volume target is provisioned in sequence 6). The transcript adapter depends on how omp stores transcripts (confirmed by the sequence-1 spike).
description.testTarget: T1 Mac AND T2 no-GPU Linux VM (Lima/UTM or Vast.ai CPU) — the darwin-ism grep audit and the loop cycle MUST run on the Linux VM to prove portability; macOS side confirms detect-and-branch no-ops correctly. No GPU.

stories.summary: One Ready issue -> merged PR, headless, open model (MVP independence proof)

description.background: The Phase-1 exit milestone and the PRD independence proof: makato-oss autonomously drives a real issue to a merged PR on an open model with no human present. Composes the dispatch seam (sequence 2), model config (sequence 3), and portability (sequence 4).
description.scope: Run the full loop against one Status=Ready issue and confirm build -> review -> PR -> merge with no approval-prompt stall (sub-agents included) and the board advancing to Done. Open-endpoint dependency (resolves the vLLM circularity): sequence 5 runs against an open-model endpoint that need not be the on-instance vLLM — a cloud open-model API is acceptable for the MVP proof, since on-instance vLLM provisioning lives in sequence 8. Verify the production Claude Code makato is untouched and still functional (version fallback intact, DoD).
description.testTarget: T1 Mac OR T2 no-GPU Linux VM via omp against a cloud open-model API. Vast.ai GPU is NOT required — cross-platform (D6) means the MVP proof runs anywhere omp runs. The version-fallback smoke-test runs on the macOS host (production makato lives there). The on-instance-vLLM production topology is proven separately in sequence 8.

stories.summary: Survive Vast.ai preemption: persistent volume + reconcile-before-resume

description.background: A Vast.ai spot preemption or a destroy+recreate GPU upgrade can kill the instance mid-run. Non-regenerable state (workflow-state, worktrees, uncommitted branches) must survive on a persistent volume, and reconcile must run against GitHub before resuming (D7).
description.scope: Provision the persistent-volume layout for non-regenerable state and point the config-driven paths at it. Add the supervisor unit (systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS) with Restart=always and boot-time auto-resume. Implement the D7 reconcile decision table before resume: PR+CI green->resume from merge; PR+CI red->resume from fix; PR+CI running->bounded-timeout wait then degrade; PR absent/ambiguous->abort + board-reset to Ready (reuse issue-to-project reconcile + _reset_board_card_to_ready). Enforce the poison-pill invariant: an ambiguous phase=pr never permanently blocks the queue. The bounded-timeout value is a concrete build-phase parameter. Note: the destroy+recreate volume-reattach case (A4) must be drilled once manually before Phase 2 closes; kill-9 + supervisor restart approximates the common preemption case.
description.testTarget: T2 no-GPU Linux VM with a persistent volume + systemd — the common preemption case is simulated via process kill + supervisor restart (no GPU, no real spot interruption). ONE manual destroy+recreate + volume-reattach drill on an actual Vast.ai instance (T3-class, but any small persistent-volume instance) is required before Phase 2 closes to prove A4.

successScenarios.title: Simulated mid-build preemption resumes and completes in-flight work
successScenarios.given: a po-agent is mid-build with uncommitted changes in a worktree on the persistent volume and the supervisor is configured Restart=always
successScenarios.when: the omp process is killed and the instance reboots
successScenarios.then: the supervisor restarts the loop, reconcile runs the D7 table, the in-flight work resumes, and the PR is eventually merged
and: the worktree and uncommitted branch files are intact on the persistent volume post-restart

successScenarios.title: Ambiguous phase=pr board-resets; the queue is never permanently blocked
successScenarios.given: workflow-state contains phase=pr but no matching open PR exists on GitHub (API-stall poison-pill)
successScenarios.when: reconcile runs the D7 table on boot
successScenarios.then: reconcile selects abort + board-reset, the issue Status returns to Ready, and the next tick picks it up
and: the loop log confirms the poison-pill was detected and reset, not skipped indefinitely

successScenarios.then: the worktree directory and staged changes are accessible at the same config-driven path after recreate

outOfScope: Network-partition / offline continuation (sequence 7 — a different failure mode)

definitionOfDone: A simulated preemption resumes on reboot via the supervisor and either completes the work or safely board-resets per the D7 table
Uncommitted worktree work survives on the persistent volume across the preemption
An ambiguous phase=pr state never permanently blocks the queue (poison-pill invariant holds)
The destroy+recreate volume-reattach case is drilled once before Phase 2 closes

externalDependencies.description: Persistent volume must survive spot preemption and destroy+recreate (A4)

stories.summary: Offline continuation: local board mirror + bidirectional sync daemon

description.background: The loop reads the board live every tick; with no connectivity outside the container it stalls. A local board-Status mirror lets the loop keep dispatching offline; a sync daemon reconciles both directions on reconnect (D18). This is a distinct failure mode from sequence 6 (partition of a running instance vs a crash) and maps to design.md Critical Test Scenario #4.
description.scope: Add the mirror file (board item-Status snapshot on the persistent volume) and route loop.sh board reads through it, sharing the gh board-read primitives with reconcile. Add the sync daemon: GitHub->mirror refresh plus queued mirror-write->GitHub push of status transitions, last-writer-wins (single operator). Sync cadence + conflict rule are a tracked build-phase item (Q-mirror); the no-Status-lost assertion is locked once that is set.
description.testTarget: T2 no-GPU Linux VM — the partition is simulated via iptables -A OUTPUT -d github.com -j DROP; reconnect via iptables -D. No GPU, no Vast.ai needed.

successScenarios.title: Loop dispatches from the local board mirror during a full network partition
successScenarios.given: the local mirror is populated, the loop is running, and all outbound GitHub connectivity is blocked
successScenarios.when: the loop attempts its next board-poll tick
successScenarios.then: the loop reads from the local mirror (not GitHub) and dispatches the next Ready issue; no board-poll error halts the queue
and: loop-status.json shows the dispatch count incrementing during the partition

successScenarios.title: Sync daemon reconciles both directions and no board Status is lost on reconnect
successScenarios.given: status writes were queued during the partition and the GitHub board is stale
successScenarios.when: connectivity is restored
successScenarios.then: the sync daemon pushes queued writes to GitHub, the board Status matches what the mirror recorded, and no update is silently dropped

successScenarios.title: Stale mirror is corrected within one sync cycle
successScenarios.given: an issue moved to Done on GitHub during the partition while the mirror still shows Ready
successScenarios.when: the sync daemon runs its first reconcile after reconnect
successScenarios.then: the mirror updates to Done and the loop does not re-dispatch the already-done issue

definitionOfDone: During a simulated partition the loop keeps dispatching from the local mirror and queues status writes
On reconnect the sync daemon reconciles both directions with no board Status lost
A stale mirror entry is corrected within one sync cycle (no re-dispatch of a Done issue)
The sync cadence + last-writer-wins conflict rule (Q-mirror) are decided and recorded

stories.summary: Co-located dev stack + on-instance vLLM + unified Langfuse (one container, two projects)

description.background: One Vast.ai A6000 instance hosts makato-oss, the sagibeast dev stack, and the open-LLM engine within separate VRAM/RAM budgets (D8). A single Langfuse container with two projects (makato + sagibeast) eliminates the current devVM:3333 vs testbox:3000 port/tunnel collision (D10). This story also stands up the on-instance vLLM engine that becomes the production open endpoint, resolving the vLLM dependency that sequence 5 deferred to a cloud endpoint. It has no external dependency (distinct from sequence 9).
description.scope: Provision the co-located instance; stand up the open-LLM engine (vLLM AWQ, serving config, health-check) and wire its endpoint into models.yml. Deploy one Langfuse container with two projects and OTLP config; provision and inject each project's OTLP ingest key into the omp dispatch env. Verify the three services coexist within the separate VRAM (A6000 48GB) and RAM (>=32GB sagibeast) budgets. No end-to-end Playwright run here (that is sequence 9).
description.testTarget: T3 Vast.ai A6000 GPU instance — the ONLY GPU-required story. This is where the on-instance vLLM production endpoint is first proven and where the co-located sagibeast + unified Langfuse live. After this lands, the T1/T2 cloud-endpoint stand-in from earlier stories can be re-pointed at the on-instance vLLM.

stories.summary: Per-step success metrics across an open-only run

description.background: The manual model-switch decision (D5) and the phase quality decision (D9) both rest on measurable per-step success. This story instruments the D11 hard signals (A) and the indirect plan measurement (B) into Langfuse across an open-only run, plus the per-step modelRole->endpoint tag so open-vs-closed coverage is countable.
description.scope: Emit per-step hard-signal flags to Langfuse: build-verify gate result, CI green/red, review CRITICAL count, coder retry count, resolve-pr-conflict HALT rate, PR merged-without-override. Tag each step with its modelRole and endpoint. Derive the indirect plan-success signal (did the plan lead to a first-pass CI-green PR?). Requires the Langfuse container from sequence 8.

Each step trace carries a modelRole->endpoint tag so open-vs-closed coverage is countable
The indirect plan-success (first-pass CI-green) signal is derivable per issue in Langfuse

stories.summary: Closed-model LLM-judge + manual model-switch of one role

description.background: The trustworthy quality layer: a Langfuse native LLM-judge scores step outputs on a closed model (D12), and the operator manually switches one modelRole open->closed based on the metrics (D5 revised — a manual, metrics-driven decision, NOT automatic runtime escalation).
description.scope: Configure a Langfuse native LLM-judge evaluator on a closed-model endpoint (with its API key as an instance secret) and surface its score per trace. Verify the manual model-switch: editing one role's baseUrl in models.yml to a closed endpoint routes only that role to the closed endpoint on the next dispatch, with every other role unaffected and the switch visible in workflow-state and the Langfuse trace.
description.testTarget: T3 Vast.ai A6000 instance for the judge (needs the sequence-8 Langfuse + the sequence-10 baseline). The model-switch config flip itself is verifiable anywhere omp runs (T1 Mac included) — the closed endpoint is a remote API, so no GPU is needed for that half.

successScenarios.title: Closed-model LLM-judge score is visible per trace
successScenarios.given: a Langfuse native LLM-judge evaluator is configured with a closed-model endpoint and at least one completed makato-oss trace exists
successScenarios.when: the evaluator runs against the trace
successScenarios.then: a judge score is visible on the trace attributed to the closed-model evaluator, not to any open-model step

successScenarios.title: Flipping one modelRole open->closed re-routes only that step on next dispatch
successScenarios.given: models.yml has all roles on the open endpoint
successScenarios.when: the operator edits exactly one role's baseUrl to a closed endpoint and the next dispatch runs
successScenarios.then: only that role's LLM calls hit the closed endpoint, all other roles stay on the open endpoint, and the switch shows in workflow-state and the Langfuse trace

successScenarios.title: A closed endpoint unavailable for one role does not affect other roles
successScenarios.given: one modelRole points at an unreachable closed endpoint
successScenarios.when: a dispatch exercises that role
successScenarios.then: only that step fails or falls back per error-handling; all other steps complete on the open endpoint and the loop does not halt the queue

outOfScope: Automatic runtime open->closed escalation (rejected, D5 revised)
Version fallback to the whole Claude Code makato (D3 — a different level than model-switch)

definitionOfDone: A Langfuse LLM-judge on a closed model scores step outputs and the score is visible per trace
Switching one modelRole open->closed re-routes only that step on the next dispatch, no other step affected
An unreachable closed endpoint for one role degrades only that step and never halts the queue

externalDependencies.description: Closed-model API key for the LLM-judge and any switched role
